title: Rounding of Promotional Interest Owed on Fee-Bearing Savings Accounts
content:
How the promotional interest owed on an account of Savings & Money Market Accounts is rounded follows the fee history of the account: the count of fee entries posted to it in the three calendar months ending on the correction date.

1. Where 5 or more fee entries posted in that window, the interest owed is rounded half up to the whole dollar.
2. Where 3 or 4 fee entries posted in that window, the interest owed is truncated to the dime.
3. Where fewer than 3 fee entries posted in that window, the interest owed is rounded half up to the cent.

### The same figure under each rule

Take a hypothetical interest owed, before rounding, of 54.3561 USD.

| Fee entries in the window | Rounding applied | Figure |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 5 or more | half up to the whole dollar | 54.00 USD |
| 3 or 4 | truncated to the dime | 54.30 USD |
| fewer than 3 | half up to the cent | 54.36 USD |

Truncation to the dime discards what lies below the dime rather than rounding it, so 54.3561 USD becomes 54.30 USD and not 54.40 USD. Rounding half up to the whole dollar takes 54.3561 USD to 54.00 USD, while a figure of 54.5000 USD would go to 55.00 USD.

### Boundary of the counts

A count of exactly 5 fee entries falls in the first rule, a count of exactly 3 in the second, and a count of 2, 1 or 0 in the third.
